larger rivers downstream.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued May 30 at 2:52PM EDT until May 30 at 4:45PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...A portion of southern Mecklenburg County.

* WHEN...Until 445 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
River or stream flows are elevated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 252 PM EDT, Heavy rain due to thunderstorms caused rises
on small creeks and streams which are now draining into
larger rivers downstream. Automated gauges indicate Fourmile
Creek has risen out of its banks near Elm Lane, though the
creek has crested in its headwaters near Matthews. The main
impact will be flooding of low-lying areas such as the
Fourmile Creek Greenway and possibly some yards of homes
along Stevens Ridge Rd.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
South Charlotte and Pineville.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
When it is safe to do so, please report flooding or landslides
threatening roads or property to the National Weather Service
Greenville-Spartanburg by calling toll free, 1, 800, 2 6 7, 8 1 0 1,
by posting on our Facebook page, or via X using hashtag NWSGSP. Your
message should describe the specific location where impacts occurred
and the depth of flooding observed.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

feet this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage just
after midnight tonight.

slopes of the Bighorn Mountains, and the Robertson Draw and East
Side burn areas south of Red Lodge, could experience flash
flooding and debris flows. Stay alert!
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

action should a Flash Flood Warning be issued.
